summary: Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies under Roderick S. Bucknell by ~1993 and held a post at the University of Sydney.

Edward Garrett is a linguist and Tibetologist who completed his PhD at UCLA (~1995–2001) supervised by Carson Schütze and Dominique Sportiche. He held research assistant posts at UCLA (1996–2000) and the University of Virginia (2000–2001).

Edward Granville Browne was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Pembroke College, Cambridge (~1879–1884), and served as the Adams Professor of Arabic at the University of Cambridge from 1902.
Sinologist Edward H. Schafer studied at UCLA (~1934–1936), Harvard (~1940–1941), and UC Berkeley (~1936–1947). He served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley from ~1947 to 1984.

Edward James Rapson specialized in Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. Educated at St John's College, Cambridge, he held posts at the British Museum (~1887–1906), University College London (~1903–1925), and Cambridge as professor of Sanskrit (~1906–1936).

Edward Joseph Thomas worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of St Andrews (~1893–1897) and held posts as a professor at the University of Cambridge and at the Cambridge University Library (~1910–1939).

Edward Seidensticker was a scholar of Japanese studies who studied at the University of Colorado, Harvard, and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Stanford University (~1962–1966), the University of Michigan (~1966–1977), and Columbia University (~1977–1991).

Edward Washburn Hopkins specialized in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Columbia and earned his PhD at Leipzig (1881), later holding posts at Columbia (1881–1885), Bryn Mawr (1885–1895), and Yale University (1895–1926).

Edward Winslow Bastian works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa by 1980 and studied and served as a research scholar at Banaras Hindu University.

Edwin Arnold was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He was educated at King's School, Rochester, King's College London (~1847–1850), and the University of Oxford and University College, Oxford (~1850–1854).

Edwin F. Bryant is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Columbia University (~-1997) and held academic posts at Harvard University (~1997–2003) and Rutgers University (from ~2003).

Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (~-1861), served as Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (~1888–1890), and was President of the Asiatic Society in 1888.

Edwin Gerow is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Professor of Religion and Humanities at Reed College (~1985–2006) and was Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of the American Oriental Society (~1985–2004).

Edwin Whitfield Fay worked in linguistics and Indology, earning degrees at Rhodes College and Johns Hopkins University. He held academic posts at the University of Michigan (~1890–1891) and as a professor at Washington and Lee University (~1893–1899).
Egaku Maeda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~-1952). He held academic posts at Meijo University and as a professor at Aichi Gakuin University.

Eiichi Kimura was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1927–1930), he held posts at Osaka University (~1949–1970) and Otemon Gakuin University (~1970–1980).
Eiichi Yamaguchi works in the fields of Indology and philosophy. He was educated as a graduate student at Kyushu University, where he also held a post as a research assistant.
Eikan Taki is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Seitatsu Matsunami and held a post as a member at Taisho University.

Eiki Hoshino is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University (~1962–1966), where he later served as Professor in the Faculty of Humanities and Director (~1988–2013).
Eisaku Okada works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Kyoto University and held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science, Koyasan University, and Kyoto University.
